Chapter 7: Crafting a Standout Application and Personal Brand
Now that you’ve picked up some new skills and you know exactly where you want to go, it’s time to show the world what you’re made of. In today’s job market, making your application stand out—and building a strong personal brand—can make all the difference.
Let’s start with your resume and cover letter. It’s not just about swapping out a few keywords. Take the time to really understand each employer’s needs. Then, highlight the experiences and achievements that matter most to them. For example, instead of saying “responsible for sales,” you might say something like, “increased sales by 20% through targeted outreach,” or, “led a team to finish a project ahead of schedule.” These details help paint a vivid picture of your impact.
But there’s more to it than just great applications. Your personal brand is the story you share about who you are and what you bring to the table. And it doesn’t stop with your resume—it’s woven into your LinkedIn profile, your personal website, and even the way you interact online.
Here are a few things to focus on:
First, your professional summary. This is a short, punchy statement right at the top of your resume or online profile. It should capture your unique strengths and where you want your career to go.
Next, keep your message consistent. Make sure your resume, cover letter, and online profiles all tell a clear, unified story about your skills, values, and what you’re aiming for.
And if you can, put together a simple portfolio of your best work. It could be design samples, writing, presentations, or project summaries—anything that shows what you do best.
Think of your personal brand like a lighthouse. In a sea of applicants, it helps employers spot you—and see exactly why you’d be a great addition to their team. So be real, be specific, and focus on what sets you apart.
Don’t forget the basics, either. Clean design, error-free writing, and a professional tone go a long way toward making a great first impression. If you can, ask a trusted friend or mentor to look over your materials. Sometimes, a fresh set of eyes can catch things you might have missed.
And remember, your application is just the opening of the conversation. Be ready to dig deeper in interviews, sharing stories and examples that bring your experience to life.
That’s how you craft an application and personal brand that truly stands out.
